$comment: Catalog of selectable aka-claude-tools additions. Drives the installer menu and documents the payload. 'recommended' additions are pre-selected at the install prompt. Not listed here on purpose: hooks/integrity-check.ts, an internal SessionStart hook (like the plugin's preflight.sh) that install.sh places with any bun hook and removes with the last one; it checks the profile against the .aka-integrity.json manifest the installer writes.

additions.name: Secure base settings
additions.description: Deny-reads on credential paths (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychains, …) plus conventional env/attribution defaults. Always safe to layer on. Nonessential-traffic opt-outs (telemetry/error-reporting/feedback) are NOT here. They live in the opt-in `telemetry-off` addition, so Remote Control works by default.

additions.name: sandbox
additions.prompt: sandbox: enable Claude Code's native OS-level sandbox (changes Bash behaviour in every session)?
additions.description: Opt-in: turns on Claude Code's native sandbox (sandbox.enabled, sandbox-exec on macOS / bwrap on Linux) so Bash and every other tool run confined at the OS level, not just the Read tool's own deny rules — closing the gap where a Bash `cat ~/.aws/credentials` bypasses a Read-tool-only deny. Deliberately does NOT also write sandbox.filesystem.denyRead: Claude Code's own documented schema for that field already merges settings.base.json's `Read(...)` credential-deny rules into the sandbox's effective filesystem denylist at runtime, with the correct permission-rule glob resolution — a kit-written denyRead containing the same `Read(<path>)` strings verbatim would instead be re-resolved under sandbox.filesystem's own narrower path rules (a no-prefix glob like `**/.env` would resolve relative to the settings file root, not project-relative, and silently protect nothing). Ships off by default because it changes runtime behavior for every Bash call and needs a platform dependency: always supported on macOS, requires `bwrap` on PATH on Linux (skipped with a notice if absent), skipped on any other platform. Deliberately narrow otherwise too: does not set `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` and does not touch `sandbox.network` — those remain the operator's own call. A pre-existing `sandbox.enabled` value is stashed and restored if you later deselect this addition.

additions.name: leak-guard
additions.prompt: leak-guard: block secrets + internal identifiers in WEB queries [bun]?
additions.description: PreToolUse guard on WebSearch/WebFetch and the SearXNG MCP tools (WEB egress only, Bash egress is command-guard's surface). Blocks web queries/urls/prompts containing detected secrets (trufflehog), token/SSH-key shapes, and (if configured) your org's internal identifiers (CT_EGRESS_PATTERNS, read from the install-compiled org-egress.json sidecar, portable-subset regex only). Covers the SearXNG MCP surface so secure-deep-research's sensitive-topic path (routed through self-hosted SearXNG for privacy) is egress-scanned too (a no-op when no SearXNG server is configured). Runs under bun (like command-guard), a hard dependency: selecting leak-guard aborts the install if bun is absent, rather than shipping a default-on security guard silently disabled. Depth: this matches secret and key SHAPES on egress, not PII/PHI/financial data, and it blocks rather than redacts. It is claude-tools' shallow secret-scan fallback; deep content detection with redaction and an audit trail is ai-tc's job. The two compose: posture here, detection in ai-tc.

additions.name: command-guard
additions.prompt: command-guard, the sole Bash egress guard: credential exfil, curl|bash, startup-file writes, internal identifiers [bun]?
additions.description: PreToolUse guard on Bash, the SOLE Bash egress guard (leak-guard is web-only). Denies pipe-to-shell (curl | bash) and writes to shell startup files (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, …, a persistence vector the secure-settings Edit/Write deny can't reach via a Bash redirection). On outbound commands (curl/wget/nc/…) it denies a detected secret (trufflehog), an org internal-identifier match (CT_EGRESS_PATTERNS via the shared sidecar), and a credential key-shape paired with the outbound tool. Alerts on nc/socat/sendmail/env-dump/inline-interpreter. Requires bun, a hard dependency: selecting command-guard aborts the install if bun is absent, rather than shipping a default-on security guard silently disabled. Depth: the exfil tier matches secret and credential key SHAPES, not PII/PHI/financial data, and blocks rather than redacts; the structural denies (pipe-to-shell, startup-file writes) are posture, not content detection. This is claude-tools' shallow fallback; deep content detection is ai-tc's job. The two compose: posture here, detection in ai-tc.

additions.name: mcp-guard
additions.prompt: mcp-guard: MCP server allow/deny policy + secrets in MCP tool inputs [bun]?
additions.description: PreToolUse guard on every MCP tool (mcp__*). Applies your MCP server policy first: CT_MCP_DENY blocks the named servers, and a non-empty CT_MCP_ALLOW blocks every server not on it (comma-separated server names, case-insensitive, read from the install-compiled mcp-policy.json sidecar). Then scans the whole tool input, keys and values at any depth, for token/SSH-key shapes and (if configured) your org's internal identifiers (CT_EGRESS_PATTERNS). Regex tiers only: it runs on every MCP call, so trufflehog stays on the Bash and web egress guards, for latency. Input too large or too deeply nested to scan is blocked, not passed. Requires bun, a hard dependency: selecting mcp-guard aborts the install if bun is absent, rather than shipping a default-on security guard silently disabled. Depth: this matches secret and key SHAPES, not PII/PHI/financial data, and it blocks rather than redacts. When ai-tc is installed it covers MCP content detection, so the scan defers to it, while the server policy still applies. The two compose: posture here, detection in ai-tc.

additions.name: post-guard
additions.prompt: post-guard: redact secrets from tool output + warn on prompt-injection markers before the model sees them [bun]?
additions.description: PostToolUse guard on Read, WebFetch, WebSearch and every MCP tool's (mcp__*) OUTPUT, not its input. Redacts credential-shaped values (the same shared pattern set as command-guard/leak-guard/mcp-guard) from a file read, a fetched page, a search result, or an MCP tool's returned content, rewriting the tool's output before the model ever sees it. A PostToolUse hook can't block a call that already ran, so this addition never denies anything; it either rewrites the output or passes it through unchanged. Also warns (via Claude Code's systemMessage channel, never a block) when fetched, searched, or MCP-returned content contains a prompt-injection phrasing marker ("ignore previous instructions", …) — content the agent didn't author and should treat as untrusted data; the same warning is also passed to the model itself as additional context. An MCP resource block's own text is scanned and redacted like any other text content; only an image block's data and a resource's binary blob field are never scanned and pass through untouched. Requires bun, a hard dependency: selecting post-guard aborts the install if bun is absent, rather than shipping a default-on redaction guard silently disabled. When ai-tc is installed and its own PostToolUse hook already covers a tool (Read and WebFetch under Claude Code), this addition defers redaction to it for that tool; WebSearch and mcp__* are never covered there, and the injection-marker warning always runs regardless.

additions.name: prompt-guard
additions.prompt: prompt-guard: warn (never block) on prompt-injection phrasing, credential exfil pairing, and encoded shell blobs in what YOU type [bun]?
additions.description: UserPromptSubmit hook that scans the prompt you just typed, not a tool call: a prompt-injection marker ("ignore previous instructions", …), a credential value paired with a send/post/upload verb (using the shared secret-patterns corpus), and a base64/hex blob that decodes to a shell command. WARNS ONLY — it never blocks, never edits your prompt, and never adds anything to the model's context; the warning surfaces to you via Claude Code's systemMessage channel. Opt-in and off by default because it is a heads-up for content YOU authored, not an egress boundary like the other guards. Requires bun, like the other bun hooks in this kit (a missing bun aborts the install if selected, the same as command-guard/leak-guard/mcp-guard/statusline/rtk-safe, rather than embedding an unresolvable interpreter path); once installed, a runtime failure of any kind here degrades to silence, never to a block. When ai-tc is installed and enabled for this profile it narrows to the injection-marker check alone, deferring the rest to ai-tc's own prompt-content detection.

additions.name: rtk-safe
additions.prompt: rtk-safe: conservative rtk rewrites for token savings [bun; needs rtk >= 0.49.0]?
additions.description: PreToolUse rewrite on Bash; requires bun and stable rtk >= 0.49.0. Rewrites supported standalone commands, including grep and rg, which keep their native flags, exit codes, and regex dialect. Leaves alone: head (rtk read --max-lines is not a head equivalent), anything carrying a shell operator or substitution, and any command with a standalone -h/--help (rtk's own parser would answer with its usage). Preserves project scripts, package-manager runners, and interpreter selection. Inert when rtk is absent, old, prerelease, or its version check fails. Installs read-only display-command approvals including rtk grep and rtk rg; find, git branch, and mutating/egress forms retain normal permission checks. The rtk rg approval REQUIRES command-guard, which blocks ripgrep's --pre/--hostname-bin/RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH exec vectors.

additions.name: Responsive status line
additions.description: Width-adaptive status line (git, context, usage). Resolves its own config dir, so it works in any isolated config folder. Runs under bun (a hard dependency of this addition, like command-guard), not a security boundary, so the bun requirement is acceptable.

additions.name: /wrap-up
additions.description: Repo-agnostic end-of-session handoff that PREPARES, never executes: summarize, verify (stop on failure), stage intentionally with a secret/artifact scan (or just propose the git add commands), draft a conventional commit message. Multi-user aware: leaves others' staged changes alone, stops over in-progress rebases, proposes a feature branch instead of working on main. Never commits, merges, or pushes unless explicitly asked.

additions.name: secure-deep-research
additions.prompt: secure-deep-research (privacy-aware research with per-claim adversarial verification)?
additions.description: Deep-research workflow with per-claim adversarial verification: search -> fetch -> 3-vote verify -> cited synthesis. Sensitive topics are conservatively classified, query-redacted, GATED for confirmation before any external query fires, fan-out-reduced, and routed through a self-hosted SearXNG MCP server (mcp__searxng__*). Normal topics use WebSearch/WebFetch at full fan-out. Model-tiered: Scope+Synthesize inherit the session model, Search/Fetch run on Haiku, Verify on Sonnet. Auto-registers as the /secure-deep-research skill. NOTE: the sensitive-topic path needs a self-hosted SearXNG MCP server. Without it, only the normal (WebSearch) path works.

additions.name: harness-pointer
additions.description: PreToolUse guard on Bash that intercepts org-configured commands and points the agent to the right approach for your environment (e.g. gh -> git). Guidance, not a security boundary. Ships OFF and empty. Most engineers want every CLI. Enable + configure via aka-claude-tools.config.

additions.name: shell-audit
additions.prompt: shell-audit (shell startup audit: aliases, secrets, persistence, git drift)?
additions.description: Read-only auditor + skill. Walks your shell rc and every file it sources (cycle-safe) and flags: hardcoded credentials (values redacted), persistence-suspicious patterns (pipe-to-shell, eval-of-fetched, DYLD/LD_PRELOAD, writes into other rc files), duplicate or dangling aliases, and git-baseline drift. A detective tripwire for the shell-startup slice. Nothing is modified. Not a substitute for launchd/cron/ssh review.

additions.name: telemetry-off
additions.prompt: telemetry-off: set DISABLE_TELEMETRY (turns OFF Remote Control)?
additions.description: Opt-in: sets DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to opt out of Anthropic operational telemetry. Ships OFF because it disables Claude Code's Remote Control (driving the CLI from a claude.ai session). The default leaves it unset so Remote Control works.

additions.name: error-reporting-off
additions.description: Opt-in: sets DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1 to opt out of Sentry error reporting.

additions.name: feedback-off
additions.description: Opt-in: sets DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND=1 to disable the /feedback command, which sends conversation history to Anthropic on demand.

additions.name: autoupdater-off
additions.prompt: autoupdater-off: set DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER (manual `claude update` still works)?
additions.description: Opt-in: sets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 to stop automatic background updates; `claude update` still works.

additions.name: feedback-survey-off
additions.description: Opt-in: sets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY=1 to disable the 'How is Claude doing?' session quality surveys (telemetry-off already suppresses these).
